briefs.why_selected: Devanagari-primary typography-led creative with two planted contradictions. The Canon has NO accepted Devanagari source (gap G1), so this brief tests whether general typographic and commercial knowledge still helps when the script-specific knowledge is missing. A Canon arm that wins here wins on hierarchy and contradiction handling, not on script knowledge it does not have.

canon_refs.label: regularity_is_the_value_and_the_danger
canon_refs.reason: "Regularity is the value and the danger" — the brief demands both traditional and modern register, and this system is the Canon's clearest statement that structural regularity buys coherence at the cost of interest, which is the trade-off the contradiction actually poses.

canon_refs.label: the_three_aspects_as_a_sequential_test
canon_refs.reason: The three-aspect sequential test (semantics, then syntactics, then pragmatics) forces meaning to be settled before form. The brief's conflict — offer most important, shop name largest — is exactly a semantics-versus-syntactics conflict and this gives a procedure for it.

canon_refs.label: specificity_as_a_credibility_mechanism
canon_refs.reason: Specificity as a credibility mechanism. The offer carries a concrete number (20%) and this system explains why concrete terms outperform general claims of value.

canon_refs.label: the_framework_is_used_as_a_filter_that_removes_material
canon_refs.reason: The framework used as a filter that REMOVES material. Directly relevant: the customer wants three required strings plus two registers in one poster.
No Devanagari or Indic typographic material was included because none exists in the accepted corpus. The Oracle arm is not given a substitute and must not pretend otherwise.

briefs.why_selected: The purest packshot brief. C1 rated this domain `present_but_application_unbound` — the Canon holds reflection physics but every binding is a physical-production candidate. This brief tests whether that knowledge helps a planner at all when it cannot be issued as instruction.

canon_refs.label: the_three_reflection_types_as_a_contrast_set
canon_refs.reason: The three reflection types as a contrast set. A glass bottle reads as glass because of how direct and diffuse reflections behave; the brief explicitly requires it to look like glass.

canon_refs.label: family_of_angles_as_a_placement_control
canon_refs.reason: Family of angles as a placement control — the single most product-relevant piece of physical knowledge in the Canon, predicting where a reflection lands on a glossy surface.

canon_refs.label: terminological_discipline_as_a_condition_of_the_theory
canon_refs.reason: Terminological discipline: the source refuses the ambiguous word "specular" and names the concepts separately. Included because the brief's demand that the label stay legible is a reflection-control problem, and vague vocabulary is how that gets fumbled.

canon_refs.label: what_illumination_is_for
canon_refs.reason: What illumination is FOR — keeps lighting subordinate to the communication goal rather than becoming an end in itself.

Alton's named light functions and working order were excluded as instructions for placing physical lights on a set, with no bearing on planning a generated packshot. Including them would pad the Oracle context with unusable words and inflate the word count unfairly.

briefs.why_selected: Person-plus-product with an opposed-register contradiction in a trust-sensitive category. Commercial communication is one of the Canon's strongest packs (six independent origins), so this is a fair test of the Canon at its best.

canon_refs.label: image_as_the_thing_actually_bought
canon_refs.reason: Image as the thing actually bought — the brief's core conflict is what image the brand projects, and this system argues the image IS the product decision, not decoration.

canon_refs.label: psycho_logic_as_a_second_operating_system
canon_refs.reason: Psycho-logic as a second operating system — why an audience's response can be reasonable without being logical. Directly bears on "serious like a bank" versus "fun for Gen Z".

canon_refs.label: why_marketing_fails_and_what_the_remedy_has_to_do
canon_refs.reason: Why marketing fails and what the remedy must do — the failure is in the message, and processing cost drives disengagement. Relevant to a single-image financial-product ad.

canon_refs.label: the_curse_of_knowledge_and_the_only_available_escape
canon_refs.reason: The curse of knowledge — a fintech company cannot imagine not already understanding investing. This is the mechanism behind most briefing failure in technical categories.

briefs.why_selected: Reference-based and underspecified: the customer cites a previous campaign the brief never describes. Tests whether a plan asks what the reference is rather than inventing a house style.

canon_refs.label: preparation_sequence_before_writing
canon_refs.reason: The preparation sequence before writing — study the product first. In this brief the "product" includes an existing campaign nobody has described.

canon_refs.label: values_held_against_style
canon_refs.reason: Values held against style, including the culture of obsolescence and the argument for retouching an established mark rather than replacing it. The brief's whole request is continuity with something that already works.

canon_refs.label: structure_read_as_signification
canon_refs.reason: Structure read as signification — a layout structure itself signals a register, which is why "same look and feel" is a structural instruction and not only a colour one.

canon_refs.label: brand_image_is_a_personality_built_by_consistency
canon_refs.reason: Brand image is a personality built by consistency — the single claim most directly on point for a customer asking for continuity with a campaign people have learned to recognise.

briefs.why_selected: THE trade-off test of the bank. "Fast cuts for energy" versus "calm morning mood" is a direct pacing contradiction inside twelve seconds. C1 found trade-off reasoning materially better covered than the v0 map recorded; this brief tests that finding.

canon_refs.label: the_rule_of_six
canon_refs.reason: The Rule of Six — six ranked criteria for a cut WITH explicit sacrifice rules. The Canon's clearest piece of trade-off machinery, and it is included whole because a ranking with its sacrifice rules removed is not a ranking.

canon_refs.label: the_seven_general_practices
canon_refs.reason: The seven general practices, including describing the shot to set its length — pacing derived from content rather than asserted as a style.

canon_refs.label: the_attention_economy_of_the_soundtrack
canon_refs.reason: The attention economy of the soundtrack: picture and sound compete for one attention budget. This brief has a voiceover over fast cuts, so the competition is real.

Nothing on feed-native pacing was included because the Canon holds none (gap G2). All three systems concern film-length work; whether they transfer to twelve seconds is exactly what the gate should reveal.

briefs.why_selected: Multi-shot identity continuity with no dialogue, stated explicitly by the customer. Continuity is a genuinely strong Canon domain and directly relevant to a known generative weakness.

canon_refs.label: continuity_geometry_of_the_action_line
canon_refs.reason: Continuity geometry of the action line — the 180-degree arc and screen direction.

canon_refs.label: defects_with_no_within_frame_signature
canon_refs.reason: Defects with no within-frame signature. The load-bearing insight: some failures are invisible in any single frame and exist only across a pair. Essential for a running sequence.

canon_refs.label: the_four_continuities
canon_refs.reason: The four continuities — content, movement, position, sound — as a checklist across a cut.

canon_refs.label: seven_ways_to_move_attention_without_a_cut
canon_refs.reason: Seven ways to move attention without a cut. Valuable in short-form where every cut costs attention.

briefs.why_selected: Three narrative beats — need, order, arrival — inside ten seconds. The tightest compression in the bank, and the Canon has no short-form knowledge at all. Expected to expose gap G2 rather than be solved.

canon_refs.label: the_sb7_framework
canon_refs.reason: The SB7 framework — the Canon's most compressed narrative structure, and the closest thing it has to telling a complete story in very little space.

canon_refs.label: three_independent_justifications_for_cutting
canon_refs.reason: Three independent justifications for cutting — with three beats and roughly three seconds each, every cut must earn itself.

canon_refs.label: the_success_checklist
canon_refs.reason: The success checklist (simple, unexpected, concrete, credentialed, emotional, story) as a design test for a compressed message.

canon_refs.label: processing_cost_causes_the_audience_to_disengage
canon_refs.reason: Processing cost causes the audience to disengage — the mechanism that makes ten seconds hard.
No hook-window, sound-off or safe-zone material exists in the Canon (gaps G2 and G5). The Oracle arm is deliberately not compensated for this.

briefs.why_selected: A single visible speaker giving personal testimony in Hindi, in a category where credibility is the whole proposition. Tests the Canon's strongest commercial material against a spoken format.

canon_refs.label: the_salesmanship_test_as_a_decision_procedure
canon_refs.reason: The salesmanship test as a decision procedure — would a salesperson standing in front of this customer say this? A direct test for a testimonial script.

canon_refs.label: specificity_as_a_credibility_mechanism
canon_refs.reason: Specificity as a credibility mechanism. The scripted claim ("doubled my crop") is a strong general assertion, and this system argues specific evidenced claims outperform sweeping ones.

canon_refs.label: the_measurement_argument
canon_refs.reason: The measurement argument — advertising should be judged by whether it sells.

canon_refs.label: stickiness_is_a_property_of_design_not_of_subject_matter
canon_refs.reason: Stickiness is a property of design, not of subject matter.

briefs.why_selected: The densest continuity requirement in the bank — two identities, two speech turns, a specified shot structure — with an explicit register constraint ("warm, not scary") in a category where fear-based framing is the lazy default.

canon_refs.label: the_six_element_test_for_a_transition
canon_refs.reason: The six-element test for a transition — the Canon's most explicit statement that the unit of judgement is the PAIR of shots, not either shot alone.

canon_refs.label: the_four_continuities
canon_refs.reason: The four continuities, including sound continuity across a dialogue cut.

canon_refs.label: psycho_logic_as_a_second_operating_system
canon_refs.reason: Psycho-logic — why a warm framing can outperform a logically stronger fear appeal.

canon_refs.label: the_sb7_framework
canon_refs.reason: The SB7 framework, which names the internal problem as distinct from the external one. The father's "I thought I did" is an internal-problem line.

briefs.why_selected: Two contradictions at once — opposed tone, and a scope-versus-duration conflict where the stated requirements do not fit in fifteen seconds. Tests whether a plan surfaces an impossible ask instead of silently dropping a requirement.

canon_refs.label: the_rule_of_six
canon_refs.reason: The Rule of Six, again for its sacrifice rules — this brief requires something to be given up and the Canon's ranking says which things cost least.

canon_refs.label: rules_held_defeasible_by_creative_intent
canon_refs.reason: Rules held defeasible by creative intent — the Canon's own statement that its rules yield to a stated purpose, which is what stops it over-prescribing.

canon_refs.label: the_sb7_framework
canon_refs.reason: SB7, in its filter role: the framework removes material rather than adding it.

canon_refs.label: simplicity_is_finding_the_essential_core_by_exclusion
canon_refs.reason: Simplicity is finding the essential core by exclusion. Included because this brief asks for more than fifteen seconds can hold, and the resolution is subtraction rather than compression.

briefs.why_selected: A physical handoff plus Devanagari copy containing a nukta ("तेज़"), where dropping the nukta silently changes the word. Tests exact-copy sensitivity where the Canon has no script knowledge.

canon_refs.label: the_three_reflection_types_as_a_contrast_set
canon_refs.reason: The three reflection types — a uniform and a parcel are surfaces whose material must read correctly for the handover to look real.

canon_refs.label: the_four_continuities
canon_refs.reason: The four continuities across a twelve-second handover.

canon_refs.label: specificity_as_a_credibility_mechanism
canon_refs.reason: Specificity as credibility.

canon_refs.label: begin_by_searching_for_the_meaning_of_the_subject
canon_refs.reason: Semantics before form — the meaning of the required copy has to survive, which is the whole risk when a diacritic can be dropped.
Nothing addresses Devanagari orthography, because the Canon holds nothing on it (gap G1).

briefs.why_selected: The sharpest brief in the bank: an optical impossibility (necklace detail AND wide shots), an opposed register (royal Rajasthani AND contemporary), and a cultural context the Canon covers nowhere. Expected to expose gap G3.

canon_refs.label: how_tightly_the_frame_holds_the_subject
canon_refs.reason: How tightly the frame holds the subject — the exact knowledge needed to see that "show fine detail" and "shoot wide" cannot both be satisfied in one shot, and to resolve it across shots.

canon_refs.label: the_rule_of_six
canon_refs.reason: The Rule of Six for its ranked sacrifice logic.

canon_refs.label: the_three_aspects_as_a_sequential_test
canon_refs.reason: The three-aspect sequential test — settle meaning before form when two registers compete.

canon_refs.label: the_four_continuities
canon_refs.reason: The four continuities across a three-to-four shot bridal sequence.

Nothing on Indian bridal, festival or regional register was included because the Canon holds none (gap G3). This is the brief most likely to show the Canon's cultural limit, and padding it would hide exactly what the gate should surface.
